checks.invariant: The synchronous source-folder scan in create_sandbox must not starve the pool that serves agent tool calls, and its request-thread cost must be bounded; dispatch/pool separation holds.
checks.result: create_sandbox is a sync def human-only route (api.py:273-275, Depends(human_only)) running on the shared default Starlette/anyio threadpool, while tool calls run on a dedicated tool_pool ThreadPoolExecutor(32) via run_in_executor (api.py:175,317-320). So a slow scan cannot starve agent tool calls; it only occupies one default-threadpool slot shared with other human/admin routes. Scan cost is bounded by SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES=200_000 and the 10.0s deadline checked per entry inside the scandir iteration. Residual: a single blocking os.scandir()/next() on a slow or hung mount is not interrupted by the per-entry deadline, and the scan shares the default human-route threadpool; both reachable only via the human-only create route and bounded per request (hardening).

checks.invariant: scan reports complete=False whenever the list may be partial (hit cap, entry cap, unreadable dir), and the audit record keeps the count and truthfully marks a truncated list after bound_payload, which web.describe renders honestly.
checks.result: 201 instruction files -> scan returns exactly 200 hits with complete=False (0.018s). A lowered entry cap and an unreadable (chmod 0) subdir both yield complete=False while still returning the hits already found. _found_payload for 200 paths of 512 multibyte chars = 308661 bytes > AUDIT_PAYLOAD_MAX(131072): bound_payload sets payload_truncated=True and drops paths, but keeps count=200 and complete=False. web.describe then renders the count with '(목록이 길어 기록에서 잘림) (다 훑지 못함...)'. No 0-count or false-complete timeline row is possible.

hardening: create_sandbox (agentbox/api.py:273) is a synchronous handler, so IF.scan runs on Starlette's shared default anyio threadpool (distinct from tool_pool). A scan of an attacker-supplied source folder can hold one default-threadpool slot for up to the 10 s deadline; consider offloading the scan to a bounded dedicated executor.

instruction_files.scan (agentbox/instruction_files.py:160-193) checks SCAN_MAX_SECONDS only per scandir entry; a single os.scandir(d) open or the first next() on a slow/hung/FUSE/network mount is not interrupted by the deadline and would pin the request thread. Deployment-dependent and human-only; wrap the per-directory scandir in a watchdog or cancellable deadline.

_found_payload cuts each path with a character slice p[:512] (agentbox/service.py:783), so 200 multibyte paths (~308 KB) exceed AUDIT_PAYLOAD_MAX and force bound_payload to drop the whole list; count/complete survive. Enforcing FOUND_PATH_MAX in bytes would keep more paths.
